lines.trans: Yes, come in.
Hello, am I not disturbing you?
Hello. To what do I owe the pleasure?
Yesterday turned out rather awkwardly.
Indeed, not very well at all.
I brought you a bottle of wine.
And what are you doing here?
I am playing chess against myself.
I was thinking over one move for a long time.
You have two white bishops on black squares!
Listen, there is no need to interfere with my game.
Maybe we could sit down and have a drink?
I will not offend you with my refusal.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('white').

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.
With a bottle of wine in your hand?

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Послушайте, не надо влезать в мою игру.
examples.trans: Listen, there is no need to interfere with my game.

examples.text: Это слово «влезать» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to interfere' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.en: to go in, to come in, to enter

examples.trans: You go in and turn straight left.

examples.text: Входишь сразу налево, к администратору. Там сидит такой Лисицын.
examples.trans: You go in and turn straight left, to the administrator. A fellow named Lisitsyn sits there.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'yesterday' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

выпить.gloss: to drink, to have a drink

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: often used without an object for drinking alcohol

examples.trans: Oh, I've had a bit to drink now.
May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He talks for a long time.
We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

meanings.note: polite, or to several people; the first в is silent

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'game, play' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это отличная игра! Хочешь с нами поиграть? Бери карты.
examples.trans: This is a great game! Want to play with us? Take the cards.

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
Even I feel a bit ashamed right now.
It became somehow quiet in the room.
For long? You need to convince me somehow!
I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: смеяться над = to laugh at; form надо before мной

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Мы не можем его уволить. Это нехорошо.
examples.trans: We can't fire him. It's not nice.

обижать.gloss: to hurt, to offend, to bully

meanings.en: to hurt, to mistreat, to offend
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ижать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hurt, to offend, to bully', paired with 'обидеть'.

examples.text: Ребята, я понимаю, работа у вас такая. Но детей обижать нехорошо.
examples.trans: Guys, I understand, that's the job you have. But hurting children isn't right.

meanings.note: usually in short form обязан/обязана + dative + instrumental

examples.trans: You are obliged to come on time.

examples.text: Ты выпустишь меня под подписку о невыезде. И ты мне больше ничем не обязан.
examples.trans: You'll release me on a travel ban. And you won't owe me anything anymore.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Я не буду вас обижать своим отказом.
examples.trans: I will not offend you with my refusal.

examples.text: И у меня отказ от салата!
examples.trans: And I have a refusal of the salad!
What do you mean a refusal? My perfect salad?
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

помешать.gloss: to disturb, to interrupt; to hinder

meanings.en: to get in the way, to prevent

examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, greetings. Am I interrupting?

посидеть.gloss: to sit for a while; to stay (with someone)

meanings.note: посиди с ним = stay with him

examples.trans: Stay with Vika for a while.
Let's sit in a café for a bit.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

examples.text: Я долго раздумывал над одним ходом.
examples.trans: I was thinking over one move for a long time.

examples.text: Это слово «раздумывать» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to ponder' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?
Sit down and hold the door.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: 'I could eat an elephant' = I'm starving
'I could eat an elephant' = I'm starving

examples.trans: I'm so hungry I could eat an elephant!
There's an elephant at the zoo.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!
Put the chair by the table.

examples.text: А зачем нам бревно? Я вот стулья взял!
examples.trans: And why do we need a log? I brought folding chairs right here!
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: вы уж нас извините = do forgive us

examples.text: Ты уж не сердись на меня.
examples.trans: Please don't be angry with me.

examples.text: Поймите, была маленькая ошибка. Вы уж нас извините.
examples.trans: Understand, there was a small mistake. Please forgive us.

meanings.note: ход выборов = the course of the election

examples.text: Ты предлагаешь вмешаться в честный ход выборов?
examples.trans: Are you proposing to interfere in the honest course of the election?

examples.text: Подожди. Ты предлагаешь вмешаться в честный ход выборов?
examples.trans: Wait. Are you proposing to interfere in the honest course of the election?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('black').

examples.trans: Listen, look in the black cabinet.

examples.text: На нём был строгий чёрный костюм.
examples.trans: He was wearing a formal black suit.

examples.text: Как не нашла? Послушай, в чёрном шкафу посмотри. Там справа от двери!
examples.trans: What do you mean you didn't find it? Listen, look in the black cabinet. There to the right of the door!

meanings.note: играть в шахматы = to play chess

examples.trans: Do you know how to play chess?

examples.text: В шахматы умеешь играть? Я научу!
examples.trans: Do you know how to play chess? I'll teach you!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
